REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CERRITOS FINE ARTS AND HISTORICAL COMMISSION

CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the City Manager’s Office, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 3rd floor, Cerritos, CA, 90703 during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the Commission after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection at the City Manager’s Office during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to FineArts@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1311 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The Commission, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 4.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to FineArts@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the City Manager's Office no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the Commission prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Manager's Office at (562) 916-1311 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  CERRITOS FINE ARTS AND HISTORICAL COMMISSION HELD
  November 21, 2024

Regular Fine Arts and Historical Commission Meeting
November 21, 2024
City Council Chambers
Bloomfield Avenue at 183rd Street
Cerritos, California 90703

PRESENT:  Commissioner Michelle Guerrero
  Commissioner Matthew S. Kauble
  Commissioner Parimal Shah
  Vice Chair Kelly Colwell
  Chair C.J. Villaluna

1.  CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Villaluna called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. in the Cerritos City Council
  Chambers, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, California.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Chair Villaluna.

3.  ROLL CALL

  All Members of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission were present.

4.  PRESENTATIONS

4A.  Presentation to former Chair of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission

  On behalf of the Fine Arts and Historical Commission, Chair Villaluna presented a
  plaque to former Chair Shah in appreciation of his service.

5.  PUBLIC COMMENTS AND SUGGESTIONS

  Chair Villaluna invited public comments.

  There were no public or written comments and Chair Villaluna closed this portion of
  the meeting.

6.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

6A.  Thursday, July 18, 2024, 7:00 p.m., Fine Arts and Historical Commission
  Regular meeting minutes.

  MOTION: Commissioner Kauble moved to approve the minutes of the regular
  meeting of July 18, 2024, 7:00 p.m., as presented. Chair Villaluna seconded the
  motion, which carried 5-0, by roll call vote.
 7.  NEW AND OLD BUSINESS

7A.  Review and consideration, pursuant to the City of Cerritos Commission and
  Committee Scope of Authority Policy (Policy 6.02), of a Commissioner’s
  suggestion for a Commission-initiated special evaluation project for an Art
  Festival to be presented at the Cerritos Civic Center or Cerritos Center for
  the Performing Arts

  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto presented details of the agenda report.

  Discussion followed regarding bringing art tourism into the City for additional
  revenue, developing a yearly theme for the event, starting small and growing the
  event and inviting local artists to participate.

  There were no public comments on this item.

  MOTION: Commissioner Kauble moved to approve the draft specific definition and
  scop (advisory only) for a Commission-initiated special evaluation project to study
  the feasibility of the City presenting an art festival in the Cerritos Civic Center or at
  the Cerritos Center for the performing Arts and approve the transmittal of a letter
  request for authorization to the City Council per Policy 6.02.

  Commissioner Guerrero seconded the motion, which carried, 5-0, by roll call vote.

7B.  Review and consideration, pursuant to the City of Cerritos Commission and
  Committee Scope of Authority Policy (Policy 6.02), of a Commissioner’s
  suggestion for a Commission-initiated special evaluation project for the
  installation of Transformer Autobot statues at the Cerritos Auto Square

  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto presented details of the agenda report.

  Commissioner Kauble spoke about amending the original idea to the installation of
  one Transformer Autobot statue at the Cerritos Auto Square.

  Discussion followed regarding impacts to the budget, costs, avoiding making the City
  feel like an amusement park, possible public safety concerns, challenges with
  licensing the rights, the need to consider ROI, the concept being past its “prime”
  time and popularity and the fact that it does not match the culture of the City.

  MOTION: Commissioner Kauble moved to approve Option 2.

  The motion died for lack of a second.

  MOTION: Chair Villaluna moved to approve Option 1, to receive and file the report
  and take no further action. Vice Chair Colwell seconded the motion which carried 4-
  1, with Commissioner Kauble, opposed.

7C.  Review and consideration, pursuant to the City of Cerritos Commission and
  Committee Scope of Authority Policy (Policy 6.02), of a Commissioner’s
  suggestion for a Commission-initiated special evaluation project to evaluate
  the feasibility of establishing a virtual history museum

City of Cerritos  November 21, 2024
Fine Arts and Historical Commission  Page 2
   Assistant City Manager Matsumoto requested postponing this item to the next FAHC
  meeting to allow staff to expand the topic and allow for a presenter.

  MOTION: Commissioner Kauble moved to postpone this item to the next FAHC
  meeting. Chair Villaluna seconded the motion which carried 5-0.

8.  COMMUNICATIONS

8A.  Reports from Commission Staff Liaison

  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto presented details of the recent Loveland Arts
  Festival in Loveland, Colorado as well as an update of current public art projects
  including the Public Safety Memorial. Additionally, she reviewed details of the City
  Maquette Show held in the Cerritos Library.

8B.  Reports from Fine Arts and Historical Commission Members

  Commissioner Shah was excited to participate in this year’s Santa Sleigh ride.

  Commissioner Kauble asked for an update on the Public Safety Monument and
  Assistant City Manager Matsumoto provide an update and timeline for completion
  and addressed the “Milk in Time” sculpture.

  Chair Villaluna and Vice Chair Colwell commented on attending the recent Loveland
  Art Festival in Loveland, Colorado.

9.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:00 p.m.

  /s/ Kathleen J. Matsumoto
